arxiv-2106-11757.description: Abstract The memory wall bottleneck is a key challenge across many data-intensive applications. Multi-level FeFET-based embedded non-volatile memories are a promising solution for denser and more energy-efficient on-chip memory. However, reliable multi-level cell storage requires careful optimizations to minimize the design overhead costs.

arxiv-2206-01179.title: A Proof of the Goldbach and Polignac Conjectures
arxiv-2206-01179.creator: Jason R. South email: jrsouth@smu.edu August 8, 2026
arxiv-2206-01179.description: Abstract . This paper will give both the necessary and sufficient conditions required to find a counter-example to the Goldbach Conjecture by using an algebraic approach where no knowledge of the gaps between prime numbers is needed. To eliminate ambiguity the set of natural numbers, ℕ \mathbb{N} , will include zero throughout this paper.

arxiv-2307-06765.title: Sensing directional noise baths in levitated optomechanics
arxiv-2307-06765.creator: J. M.H. Gosling, A. Pontin, J. H. Iacoponi, P.F. Barker, T.S. Monteiro
arxiv-2307-06765.description: Abstract Optomechanical devices are being harnessed as sensors of ultraweak forces for applications ranging from inertial sensing to the search for the elusive dark matter. For the latter, there is a focus on detection of either higher energy single recoils or ultralight, narrowband sources; a directional signal is expected.

arxiv-2307-09809.title: Comparative analysis of Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel iterative methods
arxiv-2307-09809.creator: Pavel Khrapov, Nikita Volkov
arxiv-2307-09809.description: Abstract . The paper presents a comparative analysis of iterative numerical methods of Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel for solving systems of linear algebraic equations (SLAEs) with complex and real matrices. The ranges of convergence for both methods for SLAEs in two and three unknowns, as well as the interrelationships of these ranges are obtained.

arxiv-2308-11115.title: Exploring Parity Magnetic Effects through Experimental Simulation with Superconducting Qubits
arxiv-2308-11115.creator: Yu Zhang, Yan-Qing Zhu, Jianwen Xu, Wen Zheng, Dong Lan, Giandomenico Palumbo, Nathan Goldman, Shi-Liang Zhu, Xinsheng Tan, Z. D. Wang, Yang Yu
arxiv-2308-11115.description: Abstract We present the successful realization of four-dimensional (4D) semimetal bands featuring tensor monopoles, achieved using superconducting quantum circuits. Our experiment involves the creation of a highly tunable diamond energy diagram with four coupled transmons, and the parametric modulation of their tunable couplers, effectively mapping momentum space to parameter space.

arxiv-2309-12010.title: Convolution and Attention Mixer for Synthetic Aperture Radar Image Change Detection
arxiv-2309-12010.creator: Haopeng Zhang, Zijing Lin, Feng Gao, Junyu Dong, Qian Du, Heng-Chao Li
arxiv-2309-12010.description: Abstract Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image change detection is a critical task and has received increasing attentions in the remote sensing community. However, existing SAR change detection methods are mainly based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs), with limited consideration of global attention mechanism. In this letter, we explore Transformer-like architecture for SAR change detection to incorporate global attention.

arxiv-2506-02713.title: Open-Set Living Need Prediction with Large Language Models
arxiv-2506-02713.creator: Xiaochong Lan Jie Feng Yizhou Sun Chen Gao, Jiahuan Lei Xinlei Shi Hengliang Luo Yong Li
arxiv-2506-02713.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xiaochong Lan Jie Feng Yizhou Sun Chen Gao, Jiahuan Lei Xinlei Shi Hengliang Luo Yong Li. Living needs are the needs people generate in their daily lives for survival and well-being. On life service platforms like Meituan, user purchases are driven by living needs, making accurate living need predictions crucial for personalized service recommendations. Traditional approaches treat this prediction as a closed-set classification problem, severely limiting their ability to capture the diversity and complexity of living needs.

arxiv-2507-13963.title: Exact versus Approximate Representations of Boolean Functions in the De Morgan Basis
arxiv-2507-13963.creator: Arkadev Chattopadhyay, Yogesh Dahiya, Shachar Lovett
arxiv-2507-13963.description: Abstract A seminal result of Nisan and Szegedy (STOC, 1992) shows that for any total Boolean function, the degree of the real polynomial that computes the function, and the minimal degree of a real polynomial that point-wise approximates the function, are at most polynomially separated.

arxiv-2511-21754.title: Arc Spline Approximation of Envelopes of Evolving Planar Domains
arxiv-2511-21754.creator: Jana Vráblíková ∗, Bert Jüttler
arxiv-2511-21754.description: Abstract Computing the envelope of deforming planar domains is a significant and challenging problem with a wide range of potential applications. We approximate the envelope using circular arc splines, curves that balance geometric flexibility and computational simplicity. Our approach combines two concepts to achieve these benefits.

arxiv-2602-08914.title: Gesturing Toward Abstraction: Multimodal Convention Formation in Collaborative Physical Tasks Conference: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 13–17, 2026; Barcelona, Spain Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CH
arxiv-2602-08914.creator: Kiyosu Maeda, William P. McCarthy, Ching-Yi Tsai, Jeffrey Mu, Haoliang Wang, Robert D. Hawkins, Judith E. Fan, Parastoo Abtahi
arxiv-2602-08914.description: Abstract . A quintessential feature of human intelligence is the ability to create ad hoc conventions over time to achieve shared goals efficiently. We investigate how communication strategies evolve through repeated collaboration as people coordinate on shared procedural abstractions. To this end, we conducted an online unimodal study (n = 98) using natural language to probe abstraction hierarchies.

pmc-10507192.title: Effects of institutional rearing and foster care intervention on error monitoring and externalizing behaviors in adolescence
pmc-10507192.creator: Ranjan Debnath, Sonya V. Troller-Renfree, Charles H. Zeanah, Charles A. Nelson, Nathan A. Fox
pmc-10507192.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Children raised in institutions display deficits in error monitoring and increased psychopathology. Deficits in error monitoring might be a pathway for the emergence of psychopathology in previously institutionalized adolescents. Here we investigate the impact of early psychosocial deprivation and a foster care intervention on error monitoring and its association with internalizing and externalizing behavioral problems in adolescence A modified Flanker task assessed error monitoring in 16-year-old adolescents from the BEIP.

pmc-10644369.creator: Arvind Pujari, Byung-Man Kim, Farheen N Sayed, Kate Sanders, Wesley M Dose, Angus Mathieson, Clare P Grey, Neil C Greenham, Michael De Volder
pmc-10644369.description: Light-rechargeable photobatteries have emerged as an elegant solution to address the intermittency of solar irradiation by harvesting and storing solar energy directly through a battery electrode. Recently, a number of compact two-electrode photobatteries have been proposed, showing increases in capacity and open-circuit voltage upon illumination.

pmc-11617287.title: Variations in the milk lipidomic profile of lactating dairy cows fed the diets containing alfalfa hay versus alfalfa silage
pmc-11617287.creator: Kaizhen Liu, Meiqing Chen, Guoxin Huang, Chuanyou Su, Wenhao Tang, Ning Li, Jiyong Yang, Xufang Wu, Boxue Si, Shengguo Zhao, Nan Zheng, Yangdong Zhang, Jiaqi Wang
pmc-11617287.description: Alfalfa is primarily stored as silage or hay in livestock production. Previous research has shown that the storage method of grass significantly influences milk composition. This study aimed to investigate milk production performance and lipid composition in dairy cows fed diets consisting of alfalfa hay or alfalfa silage as roughage.

pmc-11627118.title: Can Thinning Foster Forest Genetic Adaptation to Drought? A Demo‐Genetic Modelling Approach With Disturbance Regimes
pmc-11627118.creator: Victor Fririon, Hendrik Davi, Sylvie Oddou‐Muratorio, Gauthier Ligot, François Lefèvre
pmc-11627118.description: In managed populations—whether for production or conservation—management practices can interfere with natural eco‐evolutionary processes, providing opportunities to mitigate immediate impacts of disturbances or enhance selection on tolerance traits. Here, we used a modelling approach to explore the interplay and feedback loops among drought regimes, natural selection and tree thinning in naturally regenerated monospecific forests.

pmc-11667532.creator: Mónica Rivera Mindt, Alyssa Arentoft, Amanda T. Calcetas, Vanessa A. Guzman, Hannatu Amaza, Adeyinka Ajayi, Miriam T. Ashford, Omobolanle Ayo, Lisa L. Barnes, Alicia Camuy, Catherine Conti, Adam Diaz, Bashir Easter, David J. Gonzalez, Yolanda Graham Dotson, Isabella Hoang, Kaori Kubo Germano, Gladys
pmc-11667532.description: INTRODUCTIONThe Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative‐4 (ADNI‐4) Engagement Core was launched to advance Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD‐related dementia (ADRD) health equity research in underrepresented populations (URPs). We describe our evidence‐based, scalable culturally informed, community‐engaged research (CI‐CER) model and demonstrate its preliminary success in increasing URP enrollment.METHODSURPs include ethnoculturally minoritized, lower education (≤ 12 years), and rural populations.

pmc-11674239.title: Immediate Effects of the Mandibular Muscle Energy Technique in Adults with Chronic Temporomandibular Disorder
pmc-11674239.creator: Antonio Márquez-Vera, Luis Polo-Ferrero, Ana Silvia Puente-González, Roberto Méndez-Sánchez, José Antonio Blanco-Rueda, Athanassios A Kyrgidis, Ioannis Tilaveridis
pmc-11674239.description: Background/Objectives: Temporomandibular disorders affect the muscles used for chewing, the temporomandibular joint, and other related tissues, resulting in pain, limited mobility, and dysfunction of the masticatory muscles. Physical therapy plays a critical role in treatment. Manual therapy can trigger neurophysiological mechanisms that contribute to pain relief and a reduction in muscle activation.

pmc-12504050.title: Factor XIII Deficiency: A Rare Cause of Hydrocephalus in Infancy
pmc-12504050.creator: Ahmed Alali, Thkra Meshal, Zahraa Alali, Sarah Hamed, Manar Ali, Kareem lbraheem
pmc-12504050.description: Factor XIII deficiency is a very rare bleeding disorder that can cause serious bleeding problems, especially in infants. We describe a 5‐month‐old girl who came in with a rapidly increasing head size and a bulging fontanelle. She had no fever or injury. A CT scan showed bleeding in the right side of her brain and hydrocephalus.

pmc-13108565.title: Collaboration Between People Admitted to Acute Mental Health Units, Their Family Members and Nurses in the Detection of Mental State Changes and Recovery: A Qualitative Systematic Review
pmc-13108565.creator: Karen Foster, Linda Coventry, Yvonne Middlewick, Lindsay Smith, Beverley Ewens
pmc-13108565.description: Mental health nurses can engage with people with mental health challenges and their families due to their presence on acute mental health units. This presence helps to facilitate recovery‐focused care within a physically and emotionally safe environment. Mental health care should be person‐centred, individualised, and include wherever possible family and other people in the person's support network.

pmc-13269176.title: A Generative AI Framework for Pharmacokinetic Clinical Study Report Authoring
pmc-13269176.creator: John Samuelsson, Samuel Blakeman, Ezra Alexander, Srividya Neelakantan, Ravi Shankar Prasad Singh, May Garrett, Allison Murphy, Jing Zhu, Subha Madhavan, Sheraz Khan
pmc-13269176.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Clinical Study Reports (CSRs) constitute the final consolidation of findings from clinical studies and routinely include Pharmacokinetic (PK) results. To assist with PK results authoring, we developed a generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) based method that employs a hierarchical, chained large language model (LLM) framework with in‐context learning to draft PK results directly from study Tables, Listings, and Figures (TLFs), with optional human input.

pmc-13298288.title: Modeling and Simulation of Mass Transfer in Food Processing: Recent Advances in Governing Equations, Workflow, and Applications
pmc-13298288.creator: Sihui Chen, Zhou Qin, Tianxing Wang, Junjun Zhang, Roujia Zhang, Yucheng Zou, Jiyong Shi
pmc-13298288.description: Mass transfer is central to food processing but remains difficult to quantify because food materials are heterogeneous, multiphase, porous, biologically structured, and dynamically changing. Under these conditions, experiments alone cannot fully capture the spatiotemporal complexity of transport behavior, making modeling and simulation essential for mechanism interpretation, process prediction, and engineering optimization.

pmc-13440391.title: Anisotropic variable negative-Poisson-ratio metamaterials for tunable multispectral camouflage and electromagnetic energy harvesting
pmc-13440391.creator: Xiaofen Yang, Kaixia Yang, Meiwan Ying, Zhengchen Wu, Wenbin You, Bicheng Li, Lei Wang, Liting Yang, Renchao Che
pmc-13440391.description: Adaptive electromagnetic compatibility, camouflage, and energy conversion raises challenge in the swiftly responsive modulation. Herein, we designed pixelated negative-Poisson-ratio metamaterials that enable fast control over structural anisotropy and thus electromagnetic properties. One-dimensional conductors are highly oriented in each pixel through sequential shear, stretch, and alignment processes. The uniaxial anisotropy leads to the highest conductive ratio of 2.

pmc-13662515.title: Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Length of Stay for General Surgery Patients: A Systematic Review
pmc-13662515.creator: Joshua Blum, Nomiki Glynatsis, Brieanna Hill, James Montgomery, Richard Turner
pmc-13662515.description: BackgroundLength of stay (LoS) prediction is vital for optimizing surgical patient flow and resource allocation. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models may enhance LoS prediction, yet their validity and clinical utility in General Surgery remain unclear.MethodsEmbase, Medline, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched to June 2025.
